key_insight: Recurrent neural operators can approximate microstructure-dependent homogenized viscoelastic laws uniformly over time, admissible loading histories, and material fields, with sufficient internal-variable dimension growing logarithmically in inverse relative stress error and material contrast.
engineering_relevance: These surrogates could replace costly concurrent unit-cell simulations while retaining microstructure dependence and loading-history effects.
method: Encode loading-history dependence through recurrent internal variables.
Use neural operators to represent microstructure-dependent constitutive response.
Approximate the homogenized memory kernel spectrally to prove universal approximation in 2D and 3D.
evidence_signal: Viscoelasticity and crystal-plasticity experiments examine internal-variable dimension and sample complexity, while theoretical results are formally verified in Lean 4.
watch_item: The approximation guarantees concern periodic linear Kelvin–Voigt viscoelasticity; the crystal-plasticity experiments do not establish equivalent guarantees for nonlinear inelastic behavior.
paper_title: Operator Learning of Microstructure-Dependent Internal-Variable Models for Inelastic Homogenization: Approximation and Complexity
